what_it_does: This paper introduces YOCO, a chip architecture designed to run large AI models with very high energy efficiency by doing arithmetic directly inside the memory rather than shuttling data between a separate processor and memory chips. The key idea is called in-memory computing (IMC) — instead of reading values out of memory, sending them to a processor to multiply them, and writing results back, the multiplication happens inside the memory cells themselves. YOCO uses charge-domain computation (storing a running total as an electric charge) and time-domain accumulation (counting pulses over time) to carry out 8-bit multiplications — 8-bit meaning numbers rounded to 256 possible levels, which is precise enough for many AI tasks. It pairs two memory technologies: ReRAM (resistive RAM — a type of non-volatile memory that can also act as a resistor for analog math) and SRAM (fast on-chip scratch-pad memory) to balance speed and density. The architecture also includes a specialized pipeline for running transformer models — the architecture behind most modern AI systems — more efficiently.
